reason: The hypothesis combines two distinct treatments—deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) and low-temperature plasma oxy-nitriding—that are studied in separate papers (P11 for DCT on TC4; P5, P12, P21, P24 for oxy-nitriding on TC4) into a single sequential hybrid process. No passage proposes or tests this specific combination, and the claimed synergistic mechanism (DCT-hardened substrate enhancing the load-bearing capacity of the oxy-nitrided layer) is not stated in any source. This constitutes a synthesis of findings from multiple papers into a new proposal.
copied_elements: DCT induces β→α′ martensite, increases dislocation density, refines grains, and raises hardness (P11)
Low-temperature plasma oxy-nitriding below 700°C to avoid mechanical degradation (P5)
Oxy-nitriding forms TiN, Ti2N, Ti-O-N compound layer with interconnected porous substructure that absorbs wear forces (P21, P24)
Oxygen introduction breaks continuous TiN barrier, enabling deep N/O diffusion (P12, P24)
Hardness increase factor ~3-3.5× (P33 reports 3.37× and 3.45× for laser cladding)
Friction coefficient reduction ~30-40% (P6 reports reduction from ~0.55 to 0.30; P33 reports 33.7% reduction)
